title: Gender Associations in LLM-Mediated ADHD Self-Diagnosis
abstract: arXiv:2610.33697v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) are increasingly used for medical self-diagnosis. However, the way demographic cues shape outputs in these interactions remains poorly understood. This is particularly consequential for diagnoses like ADHD, where persistent gender disparities are not fully aligned with the clinical evidence. We adapt the Context Association Test (CAT) to evaluate whether GPT-4o responds to gendered ADHD associations in a zero-shot, self-diagnostic setting. We show that explicit cueing consistently amplifies certain ADHD subtype associations while implicit cueing produces near proxy-aligned distributions. These divergences suggest that explicit demographic cues may activate bias-mitigation mechanisms that over-correct rather than eliminate bias, whereas implicit cues appear to reflect the model's default behavior. translated_title: 大语言模型介导的ADHD自我诊断中的性别关联
translated_abstract: arXiv:2610.33697v1 公告类型：新论文 摘要：大语言模型（LLM）正越来越多地被用于医疗自我诊断。然而，人口统计学线索如何在这些交互中影响模型输出，目前仍知之甚少。这对于ADHD（注意缺陷多动障碍）的诊断尤为重要，因为ADHD诊断中持续存在的性别差异与临床证据并不完全一致。我们改编了语境关联测试，以评估在零样本自我诊断的场景下，GPT-4o是否会响应性别化的ADHD关联。我们发现，显性提示会持续放大某些ADHD亚型的关联，而隐性提示则产生接近代理对齐的分布。这些分歧表明，显性的人口统计学线索可能会激活偏见缓解机制，导致过度纠正而非真正消除偏见，而隐性线索似乎反映了模型的默认行为。我们的研究结果表明，评估LLM介导的自我诊断中的性别偏见需要仔细关注（摘要在此处截断）
tldr: 本研究将语境关联测试应用于GPT-4o的ADHD自我诊断场景，发现显性性别线索会触发过度纠正的偏见缓解机制，而隐性性别线索则暴露出模型默认的性别偏见行为。
en_tdlr: This study adapts the Context Association Test to GPT-4o in an ADHD self-diagnosis setting, finding that explicit gender cues activate bias-mitigation mechanisms that over-correct rather than eliminate bias, while implicit cues reveal the model's default gendered behavior.
